findings.statement: CXCR2 tops the convergence ranking: it is up in the UC meta-analysis, has genetic support in Open Targets, and ranks 25th of 1991 genes by Open Targets association with UC [gene=CXCR2; type=rank_context; source=ANALYSIS:rank_context; rank=25]. Open Targets clinical precedence lists UC phase 2 trials of Sb-656933 and Sch-527123; the peer-reviewed records cited here are non-UC (SB-656933 in healthy volunteers, navarixin, also coded SCH-527123, in COPD), so it is an expression-led candidate with clinical-stage inhibitors but no approved UC drug.

No plasma pQTL, colon eQTL or gut cell-type eQTL instrument exists for CXCR2, so MR could not test it; this is not evidence against the gene. Mouse colitis literature exists for CXCR2 but MGI records no single-gene colitis phenotype, so the mouse direction is not curated.

Genetically higher plasma PD-L1 lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.595]), it colocalises with an IBD GWAS signal and replicates in FinnGen [gene=CD274; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; finngen_odds_ratio_per_sd=0.734]. The direction is opposite to the biopsy change (CD274 is up in UC), so PD-L1 inhibition would be predicted harmful; this is my interpretation of the beta sign.

CD274 ranks 7th among genes significant in plasma pQTL MR for UC [gene=CD274; type=rank_context; source=ANALYSIS:rank_context; rank=7]. Sensitivity check: heterogeneity across its three instruments is nominal [gene=CD274; type=mr_sensitivity; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; layer=plasma_protein; heterogeneity_p=0.0259], and Steiger direction is correct. Safety record shows no known safety events and no constraint flag.
Atezolizumab, an anti-PD-L1 antibody, was tested in a phase 3 trial in urothelial carcinoma, and Open Targets clinical precedence records no UC trials for CD274.

CXCL5 is up in UC biopsies, yet genetically higher plasma CXCL5 lowers UC risk (OR per SD [gene=CXCL5; type=mendelian_randomization; source=DATASET:MR_UKBPPP_UC; odds_ratio_per_sd=0.634]), replicates in FinnGen but does not colocalise with an IBD GWAS signal. Blood and mucosal direction disagree, and the signal may come from a neighbouring variant.

SLC26A3 is down in UC biopsies, but gut cell-type eQTL MR (OLFM4+ crypt enterocyte progenitors) says higher expression raises UC risk (OR per SD [gene=SLC26A3; type=mendelian_randomization_gut; source=DATASET:MR_GUT_EQTL_UC; layer=gut_cell; odds_ratio_per_sd=1.607]), colocalising and replicating in FinnGen; the mucosal fall is therefore likely a consequence of inflammation rather than a causal protective loss (my interpretation). No plasma instrument was available.

CXCL8 is strongly up and replicated in the biopsy cohorts but has no Open Targets genetic association with UC (genetics component zero in the ranking). Its inhibitors ABX-IL8 (psoriasis and rheumatoid arthritis trials) and HuMax-IL8 (BMS-986253, phase 1 in solid tumours) were tested in other diseases, and Open Targets lists no UC trial.

JAK2 is an existing UC target: Open Targets lists upadacitinib as approved in UC, and a phase 3 paper describes it as a selective JAK1 inhibitor effective in UC. Biopsy expression change is modest compared with inflammatory genes; no MR instrument was available.
IDO1 is strongly up and replicated across cohorts, but Open Targets shows no genetic association with UC; it is an expression-led candidate only.

CHI3L1 is among the strongest and best replicated up-regulated genes in UC biopsies, with no genetic association and no drug in the ranking, so it is a biomarker candidate rather than a genetically supported target.

caveats: Most top expression-led genes (CXCL8, IDO1, MMPs, CHI3L1, DUOXs) have zero genetic component, so their causal role is unsupported.
MR could not be run for CXCR2, JAK2 (no cis-pQTL or gut eQTL); not tested is not evidence against.
Plasma protein MR differs from mucosal protein; CXCL5 and CD274 point opposite to biopsy direction.
Only a subset of top-40 genes was queried for MR, mouse and safety within the tool budget.
